Browse our FAQ for quick answers to common questions, or contact our support team directly if you need further assistance.\n\nWe are committed to keeping your experience smooth and your device protected.
How does Kuwago detect smishing and scam messages?
What are Online Scan modes and Data Saver?
What is URL Shield and how does it protect me?

Kuwago uses a multi-layered defense to analyze incoming messages:

• Layer 1: On-Device Machine Learning — An ensemble of Random Forest and XGBoost evaluates message structure, vocabulary, and phishing patterns directly on your device without sending private data to the cloud.
• Layer 2: Online Deep Learning — A character-level Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) provides advanced cloud analysis for emerging and zero-day threats.
• Layer 3: URL Shield — Web links inside messages are inspected for deceptive domains, redirects, and known malicious hosts.

You can control how Deep Learning scans run under Settings:

• Automatic: Scans incoming messages online immediately when connected to the internet.
• When On App: Performs online deep scans only while you are actively viewing or scanning messages inside Kuwago.
• Disabled: Keeps all analysis 100% on-device using local machine learning.

• Data Saver: When enabled, online scans are paused on cellular data and only run over Wi-Fi to preserve mobile bandwidth.

URL Shield creates a lightweight, local on-device VPN service that inspects web traffic at the DNS level. If a message link or browser attempts to load a known scam or phishing domain, URL Shield blocks the connection immediately before the page can load.\n\nAll inspection occurs locally on your phone — no web traffic or browsing activity is tracked or sent to external servers.
How does blacklisting and muting work?
How do I view or remove senders from my Blacklist?

When a sender is added to your Blacklist, Kuwago automatically intercepts and silences all incoming notifications from that number or sender ID.\n\nBecause Android reserves SMS inbox deletion for your default SMS app, Kuwago prevents intrusive popups, banners, and alert sounds from disturbing you, while safely logging the threat in your History tab.

When Auto-Blacklist is turned on in Settings, any sender whose message is classified as high-risk smishing is automatically added to your Blacklist without requiring manual action.\n\nFuture notifications from that sender will be muted instantly to keep your phone quiet and secure.

1. Open the Blacklist tab from the bottom navigation bar.
2. Filter or search by sender name, risk level, or date.
3. Tap on any entry to remove them from your Blacklist and restore their notifications.

You can also blacklist or unblacklist any sender directly from their message details in the Full Analysis modal.
Why am I still getting notifications from a sender?
Why does Kuwago stop scanning in the background?
How do I report false alarms or missed scams?

If you are still receiving alerts from a blocked or suspicious sender, check the following:

• The sender may have switched to a different number or spoofed alphanumeric ID.
• Android may have disabled Kuwago's Notification Access permission.
• Check your phone's Settings → Special App Access → Notification Access and ensure Kuwago is turned ON.

Android frequently terminates background tasks to save battery, which can stop Kuwago from monitoring incoming notifications.

To ensure 24/7 background protection:
1. Open your phone's Settings → Apps → Kuwago.
2. Tap Battery and choose "Unrestricted" (or disable battery optimization).
3. Ensure notification permissions are allowed so Kuwago can alert you of incoming threats.

If Kuwago flagged a legitimate message or failed to detect a new scam:

1. Go to the Settings tab.
2. Toggle "Help Train the AI" to contribute anonymized threat telemetry, or contact us directly.
3. You can also send feedback via the "Still Need Help?" email button below.

Your feedback directly helps retrain our machine learning models for improved accuracy.

By enabling this, you allow anonymized versions of flagged messages to be securely shared with our team for use in retraining and improving the detection model.\n\nAll data is stripped of personal identifiers before submission. Your privacy is our priority.
Report harmful text messages to the authorities automatically

When enabled, messages confirmed as smishing or high-risk phishing will be automatically reported to the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) on your behalf.\n\nThis helps authorities take action against malicious senders and protects other users from the same threats.

URL Shield requires Android\'s VPN permission to intercept DNS queries. You will see a system consent dialog the first time you enable it. Kuwago does NOT inspect your internet browsing content.

When turned on, URL Shield monitors DNS queries from your device and blocks connections to sites that Kuwago's scanner has previously classified as phishing destinations.

Blocking happens at the DNS level — when your device looks up the address of a phishing site, Kuwago intercepts the query and returns "not found" before any connection is made.

This means that even if you accidentally tap a link from an old phishing SMS, your browser will show a "site not found" error instead of loading the phishing page. You will also receive an immediate notification from Kuwago explaining the block.

URL Shield only blocks sites that Kuwago has already scanned and classified as SMISHING. Sites with no scan history are always allowed through.

🔒 Privacy note: URL Shield does not log your browsing history and does not send any data to Kuwago\'s servers. All blocking decisions are made locally, using only scan results already stored on your device. Non-DNS traffic (web pages, images, videos) passes through your normal network connection completely unaffected.
